thread:
matt: Heads up — customer running POC hit 401 then 403 on /v1/embeddings after rotating keys. They say it worked yesterday. Can we swarm?

carla: Which project/org are they targeting? Any request example from them?

matt: They gave this curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-POC-REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Project: proj-xyz' \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

sashi: 401 then 403 usually means key invalid -> rotated -> then key is valid but scope/org mismatch. Ask for raw response bodies.

lee: I pulled logs — token sk-POC-REDACTED is valid but bound to project proj-alpha under org_acme. Header says proj-xyz. Server returns: `{"error":"forbidden","message":"project binding mismatch"}`

matt: Ah — customer rotated key in their CI and replaced with a deploy key for a different project. They assumed project header would let them impersonate.

carla: Quick guidance to customer: 1) run /v1/whoami with the token to see binding; 2) remove X-Redwood-Project header if you want the token's project to be used; or 3) request a token scoped to proj-xyz.

matt: Send them this command to check:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-POC-REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami
# example response: {"org":"org_acme","project":"proj-alpha","scopes":["embeddings:write"]}
```

lee: Note: if token has `embeddings:read` only, /v1/embeddings POST will 403. Scopes are strict.

carla: They asked what scope combination they should use for the POC (create + search).

matt: For creation + search give `embeddings:write,embeddings:search`. For convenience we can issue a time-limited `poc_all` scope that maps to all embedding and generate perms. Keep it short-lived.

support-bot: alert: org_acme unusual auth failures spike at 2026-03-18T14:02:11Z (count=18)

lee: Also saw their test harness retried on 401 and hammered the endpoint — they hit a burst rate limit and got 429s after the rotation. I've flagged transient 429s in the ticket.

matt: Action items for the swarm: A) Ask customer to pause test runner; B) confirm whoami output; C) confirm desired project/org and request if they want a temp poc token; D) forward security QA bits about token binding and audit logs.

carla: I'll draft a short blurb for the security questionnaire explaining token binding semantics, audit log retention (90 days for POC logs, configurable for enterprise), and KMS options for customer-managed keys.

lee: For POC credits: issuing a scoped token is fine — usage under the allocated POC quota will be covered per the AE note. Anything beyond we escalate to sales ops.

matt: I'll request a temp token: 250k tokens, rate limit 200RPM, valid 7 days. Sales ops approve?

carla: Approved as long as AE logs it in the deal memo.

matt: Sent temp token to customer with instructions to run whoami first and then re-run their suite slowly.

support-bot: note: rate spike mitigated for org_acme; 429s subsided

carla: Customer confirmed whoami shows proj-alpha, swapped token to correct one, POC passed basic embedding tests. They still want the security one-pager and a short note on scopes. I'll attach both and close the loop. :white_check_mark:
